The project

From an idea to something useful.

I developed a smart life-jacket prototype for water emergencies and flood-response scenarios. The system connects a wearable GPS and LoRa node, intermediate radio relays, and a Python rescue-station application. Its broader design goal is to help coordinate position information with drone-supported rescue.

01

Locate and transmit

The wearable firmware acquires GPS positions, buffers packets, and retains unacknowledged messages for retransmission over LoRa.

02

Relay and visualize

Intermediate nodes demonstrate store-and-forward communication. The Python application receives packets, plots recent positions, and retrieves local wind information.

03

Estimate drift

The current predictor combines recent GPS movement with wind direction using an explainable heuristic. It generates a possible short-term path; it is not a trained machine-learning model.

Current scope

The prototype includes solar-assisted power and temperature-triggered heating logic. Radio range, battery endurance, thermal performance, and drift-prediction accuracy remain to be validated. It is an educational engineering prototype, not certified rescue equipment.

Engineering in detail

A wearable node, a radio relay, and a rescue-station app

SMARTVEST-SAR is an integrated engineering prototype. Its report traces the wearable firmware, intermediate relay firmware, and Python application to show how location data move from the jacket to an operator.

Wearable sensing

The embedded firmware parses GPS fixes with TinyGPS++, reads a temperature sensor, and queues position messages. The code uses a 5-second GPS timer for bench testing and formats each packet as a device identifier plus latitude and longitude.

LoRa communication

The jacket sends the oldest queued message and waits up to one second for an “ok” acknowledgement. Unacknowledged messages remain queued for a later retry.

Intermediate relay

A relay stores unique received messages, forwards the oldest entry, and removes it after acknowledgement. This implements store-and-forward behavior; dynamic mesh routing remains a future step.

Rescue-station software

A Python/Tkinter application receives serial data in a background thread, acknowledges messages, removes duplicates, plots coordinates, and retrieves wind information through Open-Meteo.

Solar-assisted power

The integrated vest carries a solar panel and a lithium-battery subsystem. Solar charging is intended to supplement stored energy; continuous energy autonomy is not established by the report.

Temperature-triggered output

The firmware enables the heater output below a measured 25 °C and disables it at or above that value. This is a prototype control setting; independent thermal protection and fault-response testing are identified as further work.

How the drift estimate is formed

  1. Observe recent movement

    Use the two latest GPS positions to estimate a recent movement direction.

  2. Add wind context

    Combine recent movement (70%), a weighted average of up to five wind-direction samples (20%), and current wind direction (10%).

  3. Plot a possible continuation

    Generate 20 future markers, gradually turning toward the target direction. These weights and the marker count are configured heuristics, not learned parameters.

  4. Compare with a later measured track

    The report proposes comparing predicted positions with a later recorded GPS track. It documents the prediction algorithm and visualization, while identifying quantitative prediction testing as a next step.

Implementation and validation

The report provides a prototype photograph and code-level descriptions. It separates those implementation details from field performance that still needs measurement.

SubsystemSupported by the reportCurrent validation status
GPS & radioPosition parsing, packet queue, acknowledgement, retry, and relay logic.The approximately 8 km hop is a design target. Measured range, packet-delivery rate, and relay latency are not reported.
Solar-assisted powerA solar panel is visible on the integrated jacket; a battery subsystem is described.Battery endurance and solar energy recovery have not been quantified in the report.
Temperature controlFirmware switches a heater output at a 25 °C sensor threshold.The 25 °C value is a firmware setting. Independent surface-temperature and fault-response measurements are not reported.
Drift visualizationA deterministic movement-and-wind heuristic produces a projected path.The report’s trajectory illustration is a software example. No measured prediction error against field tracks is reported.

Design choices to improve

The report proposes packet sequence numbers and timestamps, a bounded buffer, relay hop limits, independent thermal protection, and a measured energy budget. The approximately 8 km radio hop in the system diagram is a target awaiting field validation.

Technical description: SMARTVEST-SAR report, Chapter 3, Sections 4.3–4.9, Chapter 5, and Appendix A. Coordination with rescue drones is the broader design goal; the report documents the wearable, relay, and desktop prototype.
